# Random number generation

{{< include _setup.qmd >}}

R's RNG is private to R: from C you draw from R's stream, you don't create
your own. The stream state lives in the `.Random.seed` variable in the
global environment, so every use from C must be bracketed by
`GetRNGstate()` (read the state in, creating it if needed) and
`PutRNGstate()` (write it back). Skip the bracket and your draws won't
advance R's stream — repeated calls return the same values, and
`set.seed()` at the R level won't make your code reproducible.

There is no C API to choose the generator or set the seed; if you need
that, evaluate calls to `RNGkind()`/`set.seed()` (see
[Evaluation](evaluation.qmd)). For distributions beyond uniform, normal,
and exponential, use the `r*` functions from `Rmath.h` (see
[Mathematical functions](math.qmd)) — they draw from the same stream and
need the same bracketing.

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
render_entries("rng", "Random number generation")
```
